newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GPT says in strong position for purchases.
newsitem.headline: GPT says in strong position for purchases.

text.p: General Property Trust (GPT) said on Thursday it was a strong position to make an acquisition, but added that some property valuations were near full value and that the trust was not looking at any specific acquisitions yet.

"In the current market (property) trusts are broadly speaking full priced relative to the interest rate market," said David Ross chief executive of GPT Management Ltd, manager of GPT. In 1996, GPT bought GEM property trusts for A$900 million.
Ross said GPT borrowings amounted to 11 percent of the trust's A$3.5 billion in assets, which mainly comprises of retail and office property.

However, Ross said the trust was not keen on making any purchase in the retail property market at the moment due to the subdued outlook for retailing. He added the trust was looking at buying into hotel and infrastructure related property.

"The sector we are not looking to expand further into is the retail area, because of the mixed outlook for retail," Ross told reporters after GPT reported a half year net profit of A$110.9 million in the six months ended June 30, 1997.

The first half profit was boosted by the GEM acquisition as the result was well up on the A$68.1 million reported in 1995/96 first half. The first half distribution was 10.4 cents per unit, compared with 10.1 cents a year earlier.
At 12.30 p.m. (0230 GMT), GPT units were three cents down at A$2.65.
